metadata.topic: Cube, Data Collection, Presentation, Security, Rules (OS-201 retake)
metadata.source_file: OneStream Design and Reference Guide (online edition); each question lists source_section and source_url
metadata.note: Written from guide text for objectives 201.1.1-201.1.5, 201.3.1, 201.3.3, 201.3.4, 201.4.1-201.4.3, 201.6.1-201.6.3, 201.8.1-201.8.2. Not covered (pages not readable online): 201.3.2 XFD data source configuration, full Report Book creation steps, Foundation Handbook chapters. Guide pages are current online versions; exam is based on 8.x.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Cube Properties
questions.question: In a multi-cube design, which cube property must be True on the cube that owns the Workflow structure?

options.A: Is Top Level Cube for Workflow
options.B: Suffix for Varying Workflow by Scenario Type
options.C: Use Parent Security for Relationship Consolidation

questions.explanation: A is correct: Is Top Level Cube for Workflow defaults to False; when True, the cube can have a Workflow structure built from it. B is incorrect — the suffix groups Scenario Types for Workflow and only becomes active once A is True. C is incorrect — a security setting for consolidation members. D is incorrect — Cube Type is an optional grouping tag.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Cube Properties
questions.question: On a cube, the Suffix for Varying Workflow by Scenario Type settings have no effect. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: The cube's Cube Type is not Standard
options.B: The cube's Is Top Level Cube for Workflow is False
options.C: No FX rate type is set
options.D: The cube's Access Group is Everyone

questions.explanation: B is correct: the suffix setting is only active when Is Top Level Cube for Workflow is True. A is incorrect — Cube Type is just a grouping tag. C is incorrect — FX settings are unrelated to Workflow. D is incorrect — Everyone is the default Access Group and doesn't disable Workflow settings.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Cube Properties
questions.question: An administrator wants to change a cube's Name and Description after the cube is in use. What applies?

options.A: Both can be changed at any time
options.B: The Description cannot be changed; the Name can
options.C: The Name cannot be changed after creation; the Description can be changed at any time
options.D: Neither can be changed without extracting the application

questions.explanation: C is correct: the cube Name (limit 100 characters) cannot be changed after creation, while the Description (limit 200 characters) can be changed at any time. A, B and D are incorrect — they misstate which property is locked.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Cube Properties
questions.question: A cube's consolidation must store the Share member results instead of calculating Share on the fly. Which Consolidation Algorithm Type fits?
questions.explanation: D is correct: Stored Share stores the Share calculation. A is incorrect — Standard calculates Share on the fly. B is incorrect — it changes elimination behavior by period, not Share storage. C is incorrect — Custom requires rule-driven logic and is not the built-in way to store Share.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Cube Properties
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Cube Type property (Standard, Tax, Treasury, Supplemental, What If, Cube Type 1–8)?

options.A: It is an optional tag for grouping cubes by characteristics
options.B: It changes how the cube consolidates
options.C: It sets the cube's default currency
options.D: It controls which Scenario Types are available

questions.explanation: A is correct: Cube Type is an optional tag that groups cubes by characteristics; Standard is the default. B is incorrect — consolidation is set by the Consolidation Algorithm Type. C is incorrect — default currency is in the FX Rates section. D is incorrect — Scenario Type dimension assignment is on the Cube Dimensions tab.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Using OnePlace Cube Views
questions.question: A calculation runs much longer for one entity than for others. What is the best first step to find the root cause in a Cube View?

options.A: Right-click and open Cell POV Information
options.B: Right-click a cell for that entity and open Data Unit Statistics to review cell counts
options.C: Drill Down on the parent entity

questions.explanation: B is correct: Data Unit Statistics breaks the data unit into counts of zero, real, derived, NoData, calculated, consolidated, translated, journal and input cells, which reveals oversized or zero-heavy data units. A is incorrect — Cell POV Information describes one cell. C is incorrect — Drill Down shows the components of a value, not data unit size. D is incorrect — it shows sessions, not data.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Using OnePlace Cube Views
questions.question: Data Unit Statistics for a slow entity shows a very large count of zero calculated cells. What does this most likely indicate?

options.B: The entity uses the wrong currency
options.C: A stored calculation is writing zeros, inflating the data unit

questions.explanation: C is correct: a high count of calculated zero cells points to a stored calculation writing zeros, which enlarges the data unit and slows calculation; filtering with RemoveZeros is the usual fix. A is incorrect — journals appear as journal cells. B is incorrect — currency affects translation, not zero counts. D is incorrect — security doesn't create cells.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Cube Properties
questions.question: In the cube's FX Rates section, what are the default Rule Types?
questions.explanation: D is correct: Revenues/Expenses default to Periodic and Assets/Liabilities default to Direct. A is incorrect — it reverses them. B and C are incorrect — the two account groups have different defaults.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Cube Properties
questions.question: A Budget scenario must translate using a different rate type than the rest of the cube. What is the right approach?

options.A: Set the Rate Type at the Scenario level for the Budget scenario
options.B: Create a separate cube for Budget
options.C: Change the Currencies list in Application Properties
options.D: Set the Translation Algorithm Type to Custom

questions.explanation: A is correct: Rate Types for Revenues/Expenses and Assets/Liabilities can be configured at the Cube or the Scenario level. B is incorrect — far heavier than needed. C is incorrect — that list defines available currencies, not rate types. D is incorrect — Custom translation needs rules and isn't required to change a rate type.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Application Security Roles
questions.question: Which Application Security Role allows a user to update FX rates?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Manage FX Rates “allows a user to update FX Rates.” A is incorrect — it updates application properties. C is incorrect — it allows modifying data, not rates. D is incorrect — it allows editing metadata in the Dimension Library.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Account Dimension
questions.question: Which Account Type should be used for headcount or square footage?
questions.explanation: C is correct: NonFinancial is for informational accounts such as headcount or square footage. A is incorrect — Balance is for balance sheet values at a point in time. B is incorrect — Flow is for income statement accounts with periodic and YTD values. D is incorrect — Group is organizational only and doesn't aggregate.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Account Dimension
questions.question: An account exists only to organize the hierarchy and should not aggregate data. Which Account Type fits?
questions.explanation: D is correct: Group is “used to make the account organizational-only and will not aggregate data.” A is incorrect — DynamicCalc calculates on the fly. B is incorrect — it is for balance sheet accounts that don't change over time. C is incorrect — it tags expense accounts.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Account Dimension
questions.question: A balance sheet account holds a value that does not change over time unless updated. Which Account Type fits?
questions.explanation: A is correct: BalanceRecurring is for balance sheet accounts that don't change over time. B is incorrect — Balance holds a value at a particular point in time each period. C is incorrect — Flow is for income statement accounts. D is incorrect — Liability tags the account type but doesn't carry the value forward.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Account Dimension
questions.question: An account is being retired but its history must stay reportable, without writing No Input rules. Which setting is used?
questions.explanation: B is correct: In Use (default True) lets you close accounts while keeping historical data, without No Input rules. A is incorrect — it makes the member read-only but doesn't mark it closed. C is incorrect — it removes the account from consolidation. D is incorrect — Group stops aggregation and would break history.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Account Dimension
questions.question: A base-level account has a stored formula, and its results must roll up to parent entities. How should Is Consolidated be set?

options.D: It cannot consolidate because it has a formula

questions.explanation: C is correct: True consolidates the account regardless of Formula Type. A is incorrect — under the default Conditional, a member with a formula is not consolidated; the formula recalculates at the parent instead. B is incorrect — it excludes the account from consolidation. D is incorrect — True makes it possible.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Financial Model Guides > Formula Types
questions.question: A gross margin percentage must be correct at every level of the hierarchy. Which calculation approach fits?

options.A: A stored calculation in Formula Pass 1
options.B: Is Consolidated = True on the account

questions.explanation: D is correct: Dynamic Calc runs on demand when the cell is displayed and is best for ratio or percentage calculations, so it is correct at parents. A is incorrect — a stored ratio would be summed by parent aggregation. B is incorrect — that would sum the percentages. C is incorrect — an account type, not a calculation method.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Financial Model Guides > Formula Types
questions.question: Which statement describes a stored calculation?

options.A: Runs during the Data Unit Calculation Sequence (DUCS), is written to the database, and parents aggregate it automatically
options.B: Runs on demand when the cell is displayed and is not persisted
options.D: Has no impact on consolidation time

questions.explanation: A is correct: a stored calculation runs as part of the DUCS, is persisted, and parent members naturally aggregate it. B and C are incorrect — they describe Dynamic Calc. D is incorrect — stored calcs add to consolidation time; volume and complexity matter.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Data Collection > Data Sources
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the Data Source types?
questions.explanation: B is correct: the Data Source types are Fixed file, Delimited file, Connector and Data Management Export Sequence; a Cube View is not a Data Source type. A, C and D are incorrect — each is a valid type.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Data Collection > Data Sources
questions.question: Data must be pulled directly from an external system's database, with drill back to the source. Which Data Source type is used?

options.C: Connector, paired with a Connector business rule

questions.explanation: C is correct: Connector Data Sources use Connector business rules, which “communicate with, collect data from, and drill back to external systems.” A and D are incorrect — both parse files. B is incorrect — it sources data from OneStream itself.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Data Collection > Data Sources
questions.question: Data already in one OneStream cube and scenario must be brought into another through a Workflow import. Which Data Source type fits?

options.B: Delimited file exported to the File Share

questions.explanation: D is correct: a Data Management Export Sequence Data Source imports the output of a Data Management export through Workflow. A is incorrect — Connectors target external systems. B and C are incorrect — possible manually, but not the built-in Data Source type for this.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Data Collection > Data Sources
questions.question: Several Workflow Profiles import files with the same layout. How many Data Sources are needed?

options.A: One, assigned to all profiles that share the file format

questions.explanation: A is correct: a Data Source can be assigned “to one workflow profile or to many workflow profiles sharing a common file format.” B, C and D are incorrect — they duplicate work the design avoids.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Using OnePlace Workflow
questions.question: A user needs to see when and how the last source file was imported for the current Workflow Profile. Where?

options.B: The Import step's View Last Log File Processed icon

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Import step's “View Last Log File Processed for Current Workflow Profile” opens the processing log for that import. A is incorrect — it lists tasks across the system. C is incorrect — it records errors, not import details. D is incorrect — Validate shows mapping and intersection errors.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Using OnePlace Workflow
questions.question: A second file must add rows to a Workflow without changing the rows already loaded. Which Load Method?

options.D: Replace Background (All Time, All Source IDs)

questions.explanation: C is correct: Append adds new rows without changing existing data. A is incorrect — Replace clears previous data for the specific Source ID. B and D are incorrect — both replace data across all time.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Using OnePlace Workflow
questions.question: During Validate, a new source account appears with a Target Value of (Unassigned). What type of error is this?
questions.explanation: D is correct: transformation errors are listed by dimension, e.g., a new account that was added but not mapped, showing the source value and an (Unassigned) target. A is incorrect — intersection errors are about invalid combinations. B and C are incorrect — they happen at later steps.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Using OnePlace Workflow
questions.question: Every member maps successfully, but Validate still fails because a customer member was mapped to an account type that cannot hold it. What error is this?
questions.explanation: A is correct: intersection errors occur “when something is not correct with the entire intersection of data,” such as mapping a Customer to an inappropriate account. B is incorrect — each member mapped. C is incorrect — parsing happens at Import. D is incorrect — not a Validate category.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Using OnePlace Workflow
questions.question: After fixing the transformation rules for unmapped members, what should the user do?
questions.explanation: B is correct: after fixing errors, clicking Retransform automatically re-validates the data. A is incorrect — unnecessary; the data is already in Stage. C is incorrect — Load can't run until Validate passes. D is incorrect — it discards the import.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Data Collection > Mapping Types
questions.question: Which transformation rule type is the most efficient for explicitly mapping one source member to one target member?
questions.explanation: C is correct: One-to-One maps a source member to a target member explicitly with no wildcards, the most efficient approach for explicit mappings. A and B are incorrect — they evaluate wildcards. D is incorrect — it evaluates a range.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Data Collection > Mapping Types
questions.question: Which rule type stops processing as soon as a record meets its criteria, making rule order important?
questions.explanation: D is correct: “Composite rules stop processing when a record meets the criteria.” A is incorrect — “Range rules do not stop processing”; with overlapping ranges, the last processed rule applies. B and C are incorrect — they map explicit members.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Data Collection > Mapping Types
questions.question: Which pair correctly matches rule type to source syntax?
questions.explanation: A is correct: Range uses ~ between lower and upper limits; List uses ; between members. B is incorrect — it swaps them. C is incorrect — * is a wildcard for Mask and Composite. D is incorrect — | causes errors in source and target members.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Data Collection > Mapping Types
questions.question: Which rule type supports the * and ? wildcards, including double-sided patterns like *000*?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Mask mappings use * and ? wildcards and support double-sided wildcards such as *000*. A, C and D are incorrect — none of them evaluates wildcards.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Using OnePlace Cube Views
questions.question: A user wants the XFGetCell formula for a Cube View cell to paste into Excel. Which right-click option provides it?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Cell POV Information shows the cell's full POV, member properties and formulas, and lets you copy an XFGetCell (Excel) or XFCell (Extensible Document) formula. A is incorrect — it shows data unit cell counts. B is incorrect — it shows component data. D is incorrect — it shows status, not formulas.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube Views > Cube View Performance
questions.question: A Cube View should hide rows that contain zeros but still show rows with no data. Which settings?

options.A: Suppress NoData Rows = True; Suppress Zero Rows = False
options.D: Suppress NoData Rows = False; Suppress Zero Rows = True

questions.explanation: D is correct: Suppress Zero Rows hides cells containing zeros; Suppress NoData Rows hides cells without data, so only the zero setting should be True. A is incorrect — it does the opposite. B is incorrect — it hides both. C is incorrect — it hides neither.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube Views > Cube View Performance
questions.question: A Cube View nests several dimensions in rows and runs slowly because most combinations have no data. What does the guide recommend?

options.C: Move every dimension to the POV

questions.explanation: A is correct: sparse row suppression is recommended when multiple dimensions are nested in rows and the report would return many records without data. B is incorrect — it makes the report larger. C is incorrect — it changes the report's purpose. D is incorrect — it doesn't address sparsity.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube Views > Cube View Performance
questions.question: When does Cube View paging activate automatically?

options.A: When the Cube View exceeds 1,000 columns
options.B: When the Cube View exceeds 10,000 unsuppressed rows
options.D: When the user opens it in Excel

questions.explanation: B is correct: paging activates when a Cube View exceeds 10,000 unsuppressed rows. A, C and D are incorrect — none is the documented trigger.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workspaces > Workspaces Properties
questions.question: Which workspace property allows other workspaces to reference objects in the current workspace?
questions.explanation: C is correct: “If this property is set to True, other workspaces can reference objects in the current workspace.” A is incorrect — that lists which workspaces this one looks into. B is incorrect — it names the service factory for dynamic dashboards. D is incorrect — it controls user access.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workspaces > Workspaces Properties
questions.question: Which statement about the Default workspace is true?

options.A: It must be listed in Shared Workspace Names to be referenced
options.B: It can only reference its own objects
options.D: It is always shared and accessible by any other workspace

questions.explanation: D is correct: the Default workspace is “always shared and is accessible by any other workspace, even if not explicitly added,” and behaves as if all other workspaces are on its shared list. A and B are incorrect — they contradict that. C is incorrect — it can contain dashboards.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workspaces > Workspaces Properties
questions.question: A dashboard references a parameter by name. In what order are workspaces searched?

options.A: Current, then Default, then Shared Workspaces in the order listed
options.B: Default, then current, then Shared Workspaces
options.C: Shared Workspaces, then current, then Default

questions.explanation: A is correct: resolution goes current workspace, then Default, then the Shared Workspace Names in entry order. B and C are incorrect — wrong order. D is incorrect — other workspaces are searched.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Workspaces > Workspaces Properties
questions.question: Workspace A must use a parameter from custom Workspace B. What is required?

options.A: Only that B is listed in A's Shared Workspace Names
options.B: B is listed in A's Shared Workspace Names and B has Is Shareable Workspace = True
options.C: Only that B has Is Shareable Workspace = True
options.D: Both workspaces must have the same Maintenance Group

questions.explanation: B is correct: custom workspaces can reference objects only from workspaces listed in their Shared Workspace Names, and only if those have Is Shareable Workspace enabled. A and C are incorrect — each is half the requirement. D is incorrect — security groups don't control referencing.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Presentation > Book Properties
questions.question: A report book should work out which input parameters it needs from its content. Which book property does this?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Determine Parameters from Content set to True automatically determines the required input parameters from the book's content items. A is incorrect — that is a manual comma-separated list. B is incorrect — it changes parameter values partway through the book. D is incorrect — it repeats content.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Data Access (Data Cell Access Security)
questions.question: HR_Comp members need All Access to actual compensation; everyone else with entity access must see no compensation. Both items use S#Actual:A#[Total Compensation].Tree. Which configuration works?

options.A: Item 1: Everyone, No Access, Apply Access and Stop. Item 2: HR_Comp, All Access, Apply Access and Stop.
options.B: Item 1: HR_Comp, All Access, Apply Access and Continue. Item 2: Everyone, No Access, Apply Access and Stop.
options.C: Item 1: Everyone, No Access, Decrease Access and Stop. Item 2: HR_Comp, All Access, Increase Access and Stop.
options.D: Item 1: HR_Comp, All Access, Apply Access and Stop. Item 2: Everyone, No Access, Apply Access and Stop.

questions.explanation: D is correct: the specific item comes first with Stop, so HR_Comp members get All Access and evaluation ends; everyone else falls through to No Access. A and C are incorrect — Everyone matches HR users first and Stop ends evaluation, so HR is blocked. B is incorrect — Continue lets HR users reach item 2, which removes their access.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Data Access (Data Cell Access Security)
questions.question: The user is in the item's group and the cell is in its filter. With no behavior changed, what happens?
questions.explanation: A is correct: Apply Access and Continue is the default when the user is in the group and the cell is in the filter. B is incorrect — Skip Item and Continue is the default when only one of those is true. C and D are incorrect — Stop is never the default.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Data Access (Data Cell Access Security)
questions.question: In a Data Cell Access item, what does “and Stop” mean?

options.B: Stop evaluating the remaining Cube Data Access items

questions.explanation: B is correct: …and Stop means “stop evaluating the remaining Cube Data Access items.” A, C and D are incorrect — Stop only affects rule evaluation.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Data Access (Data Cell Access Security)
questions.question: A user has no Read Data Group or Read Write Data Group access to Entity 200. A Data Cell Access item grants the user's group All Access to a slice of Entity 200. What can the user do?

options.C: Nothing in Entity 200; data cell rules only refine entity-level access
options.D: Read and write all of Entity 200

questions.explanation: C is correct: data cell access is a second layer after entity-level access; users need entity Read or Read Write access first. A, B and D are incorrect — they assume cell rules can grant access the entity doesn't.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Foundation Guides > Change the Relationship Security
questions.question: With relationship security on, a user sees NoAccess on the consolidation members for USClubs, though the user can read USClubs. What is the likely cause?

options.A: The user is not in the Workflow Execution Group
options.B: A Data Cell Access item uses Skip Item and Stop
options.C: USClubs has no Display Member Group
options.D: The user lacks rights to USClubs' immediate parent, NAClubs

questions.explanation: D is correct: with relationship security, consolidation members follow the user's rights to the immediate parent; NoAccess usually means no access to the parent, even if it isn't on the report. A is incorrect — Workflow security doesn't govern cube data access. B is incorrect — unrelated to consolidation members. C is incorrect — it controls display, not this access.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Cube > Cube Properties
questions.question: Which cube property turns on relationship security for consolidation members, and what is its default?

options.A: Use Parent Security for Relationship Consolidation; default False
options.B: Use Parent Security for Relationship Consolidation; default True
options.C: Is Top Level Cube for Workflow; default False

questions.explanation: A is correct: Use Parent Security for Relationship Consolidation in the cube's Security section defaults to False. B is incorrect — wrong default. C is incorrect — a Workflow setting. D is incorrect — it controls who can see the cube object.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Application Security Roles
questions.question: What is the difference between Application Security Roles and Application User Interface Roles?

options.A: Security roles control screen access; UI roles control tasks
options.B: Security roles grant permission to perform tasks; UI roles control access to specific screens and pages
options.C: They are the same roles with different names
options.D: UI roles apply only to Excel

questions.explanation: B is correct: Application Security Roles grant functional permissions (modify data, manage metadata); Application User Interface Roles control access to screens and admin pages. A is incorrect — it reverses them. C and D are incorrect — they are distinct, and UI roles are not Excel-specific.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Application Security Roles
questions.question: An administrator cannot perform a mass deletion of metadata and data. Which role is likely missing, and why?

options.A: Administer Application; it is not automatic
options.B: Manage Metadata; it is only for Excel
options.C: Administrator Database; administrators are not automatically given access
options.D: Modify Data; it is required for metadata

questions.explanation: C is correct: Administrator Database permits mass deletion of metadata and data, and “Administrators are not automatically given access.” A is incorrect — the user is already an administrator. B is incorrect — Manage Metadata edits the Dimension Library and isn't Excel-only. D is incorrect — it governs data entry.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Application Security Roles
questions.question: A user cannot see the application in the list when logging in. Which role is most likely missing?
questions.explanation: D is correct: Open Application “allows the user to see and open the application.” A, B and C are incorrect — they govern data access after the application is open.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Application Security Roles
questions.question: An audit group must view all data in the application, regardless of entity security. Which role fits?
questions.explanation: A is correct: View All Data “allows a group of users to view all data in the application.” B is incorrect — it allows changing data. C is incorrect — it is an administrator function for managing data. D is incorrect — it only opens the application.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Business Rule Types
questions.question: A source file field must be modified while the Stage Parser Engine reads it. Which business rule type?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Parser rules “evaluate and/or modify field values being processed by the Stage Parser Engine.” A is incorrect — Derivative rules derive data before mapping. C is incorrect — Conditional rules evaluate mapping criteria. D is incorrect — Connector rules talk to external systems.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Business Rule Types
questions.question: A mapping must assign a target based on a condition evaluated during transformation. Which business rule type?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Conditional rules (mapping) “conditionally evaluate mapping criteria during the data transformation process.” A is incorrect — it works during parsing. B is incorrect — it runs cube calculations. D is incorrect — it is a general-purpose rule type.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Business Rule Types
questions.question: Before mapping, new records must be calculated from source values (for example, deriving a total). Which business rule type?
questions.explanation: D is correct: Derivative rules “evaluate and/or calculate values during the data derivation process,” before mapping. A is incorrect — it runs during transformation. B is incorrect — it modifies fields while parsing, not deriving. C is incorrect — it builds query results for dashboards.

questions.subtopic: Business Rule Types — Cube View Extender
questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Business Rule Types
questions.question: Advanced formatting such as custom headers and conditional cell formatting must be applied to a Cube View in Report view. Which business rule type?
questions.explanation: A is correct: Cube View Extender rules “apply advanced Cube View formatting to any Cube View while in Report view.” B is incorrect — for dashboard actions. C is incorrect — for dynamic property values. D is incorrect — for calculations.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Business Rule Types
questions.question: A dashboard needs a programmatic query that combines several sources into one result set. Which business rule type?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Dashboard DataSet rules “create programmatic query results.” A is incorrect — it handles button clicks, uploads and actions. C is incorrect — it connects to external systems for import. D is incorrect — it formats Cube Views.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Business Rule Types
questions.question: A dashboard button must run custom logic when clicked. Which business rule type?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Dashboard Extender rules handle tasks such as button clicks, file uploads and workflow automation. A is incorrect — it returns query results. B is incorrect — it returns string values for properties. D is incorrect — it is for import parsing.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Business Rule Types
questions.question: A dashboard component property must be set dynamically through business rule logic in parameter syntax. Which type?
questions.explanation: D is correct: Dashboard XFBR String applies rule logic to dashboard component properties through parameter syntax. A is incorrect — it performs actions. B is incorrect — general-purpose, not the property mechanism. C is incorrect — it is for mapping.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Application Tools > Business Rule Types
questions.question: Which business rule type is the most generalized, including extenders for custom tasks and event handlers?
questions.explanation: A is correct: Extender (Extensibility) rules “are the most generalized type of Business Rule,” including extenders and event handlers. B, C and D are incorrect — each serves a specific purpose.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Financial Model Guides > Finance Function Types
questions.question: Certain cells must be made read-only based on logic. Which Finance Function Type?
questions.explanation: B is correct: “Conditional Input Rules make data cells read-only.” A is incorrect — it defines reusable GetDataCell calculations. C is incorrect — it builds member lists. D is incorrect — it runs with confirmation rules.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Financial Model Guides > Finance Function Types
questions.question: A Better/Worse calculation must be reused across many Cube Views. Which Finance Function Type?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Data Cell provides “named GetDataCell calculations that can be reused,” such as Better/Worse. A is incorrect — it adds logic during calculation and stores results. B is incorrect — it returns lists of members. D is incorrect — it is logic for Dynamic Calc members.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Financial Model Guides > Finance Function Types
questions.question: A Cube View needs a custom list of members built by a rule. Which Finance Function Type?
questions.explanation: D is correct: Member List returns “a custom list of members for use in Cube Views and other areas.” A is incorrect — it returns calculated values. B is incorrect — it runs during calculation. C is incorrect — it determines exchange rates.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Financial Model Guides > Finance Function Types
questions.question: Custom logic must decide which exchange rate applies at specific intersections. Which Finance Function Type?
questions.explanation: A is correct: FXRate provides “custom logic used to determine Foreign Exchange rates for any intersection.” B is incorrect — it adds custom translation logic, not rate selection. C is incorrect — it calculates the Share member. D is incorrect — general calculation logic.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Financial Model Guides > Finance Function Types
questions.question: Custom logic is needed for the Elimination member during consolidation. Which Finance Function Type?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Consolidate Elimination adds logic for the custom calculation of the Elimination member. A is incorrect — it is for the Share member. C and D are incorrect — they run at calculation and translation, not elimination.

questions.source_section: D&R Guide > Financial Model Guides > Finance Function Types
questions.question: Which Finance Function Type is designed to be run from a Dashboard Parameter Component server task action, rather than during consolidation?
questions.explanation: C is correct: a CustomCalculate function type can execute a custom calculation via a Dashboard Parameter Component Server Task Action and doesn't run during consolidation. A is incorrect — it runs in the calculation sequence. B is incorrect — it runs with confirmation rules. D is incorrect — it calculates ownership results.
